The regulated release of a prostaglandin, any of a group of biologically active metabolites which contain a cyclopentane ring, from a cell or a tissue. [GOC:mah]

The chemical reactions and pathways involving prostanoids, any compound based on or derived from the prostanoate structure. [ISBN:0198506732]

The addition of an acyl group, any group or radical of the form RCO- where R is an organic group, to a protein amino acid. [GOC:jl]
The ADP-ribosylation by a protein of one or more of its own amino acid residues, or residues on an identical protein. [GOC:BHF, GOC:rl]

The removal of palymitoyl groups from a lipoprotein. [GOC:hjd]
The process of removing one or more phosphoric residues from a protein. [GOC:hb]

The covalent attachment of a geranylgeranyl group to a protein. [GOC:jl]

The addition of a hydroxy group to a protein amino acid. [GOC:ai]
The targeting and directed movement of proteins into a cell or organelle. Not all import involves an initial targeting event. [GOC:ai]

A process of protein insertion into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane in which stop-transfer membrane-anchor sequences become an ER membrane spanning helix. [ISBN:0716731363]

Mitochondrial inner membrane proteins can get inserted from the cytosol, by crossing the outer membrane and being guided by an inner membrane translocase complex into their final destination in the inner membrane. The process in which a protein is incorporated into the mitochondrial inner membrane from the matrix side. This includes membrane insertion of newly synthesized mitochondrially-encoded proteins, and insertion of nuclear-encoded proteins after their import into the mitochondrial matrix. [GOC:vw, PMID:12880202, PMID:15473843]

K11-linked polyubiquitination targets the substrate protein for degradation. The anaphase-promoting complex promotes the degradation of mitotic regulators by assembling K11-linked polyubiquitin chains. [GOC:jsg, GOC:pr, GOC:sp, PMID:18485873, PMID:20655260, PMID:21113135]
A protein ubiquitination process in which a polymer of ubiquitin, formed by linkages between lysine residues at position 27 of the ubiquitin monomers, is added to a protein. [PMID:19345326]

A protein deubiquitination process in which a K48-linked ubiquitin chain, i.e. a polymer of ubiquitin formed by linkages between lysine residues at position 48 of the ubiquitin monomers, is removed from a protein. [GOC:mah]

A protein ubiquitination process in which a polymer of ubiquitin, formed by linkages between lysine residues at position 48 of the ubiquitin monomers, is added to a protein. K48-linked ubiquitination targets the substrate protein for degradation. [GOC:cvs, PMID:15556404]

A protein ubiquitination process in which a polymer of ubiquitin, formed by linkages between lysine residues at position 6 of the ubiquitin monomers, is added to a protein. K6-linked ubiquitination is involved in DNA repair. [GOC:sp]

A protein deubiquitination process in which a K63-linked ubiquitin chain, i.e. a polymer of ubiquitin formed by linkages between lysine residues at position 63 of the ubiquitin monomers, is removed from a protein. [GOC:mah, PMID:19202061, PMID:19214193]

[GOC:mah, PMID:15556404]
A series of reactions, mediated by the intracellular serine/threonine kinase protein kinase C, which occurs as a result of a single trigger reaction or compound. [GOC:BHF, GOC:mah]

The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of proteins and lipids to form a protein-lipid complex. [GOC:jl]

The lipoylation of peptidyl-lysine to form peptidyl-N6-lipoyl-L-lysine. [RESID:AA0118]

Any process in which a protein is transported to, and/or maintained at the adherens junction. [GOC:aruk, GOC:bc, GOC:BHF, GOC:mah, PMID:26412237]
